pr.title: feat(github): read GitHub's native stacks behind stk.githubStacks
pr.body: GitHub shipped [native stacked pull requests](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-07-30-stacked-pull-requests-are-now-in-public-preview/) to public preview. The local half of `gh stack` duplicates what git-stk already does; what GitHub has that git-stk cannot produce is the **server-side stack object** - the stack map on every PR, per-layer diffs reviewed in parallel, and atomic stack merge. This makes git-stk first-class there: git-stk stays the local driver, GitHub owns the stack. All of it is behind **`stk.githubStacks`, off by default** - the GitHub feature is in public preview, and off means today's behaviour byte for byte. GitLab, Gitea and the demo provider are untouched. ## What it does - **Reads** the stack: `NativeStack` and `ReviewProvider::native_stack_for`, with a `None` default - the same optional-method pattern as `review_state`, so only `GitHubProvider` implements anything. It shells to `gh api`, so no new dependency, no HTTP client, no credential handling. - **Registers** it: `submit --stack`/`--downstack` posts the ordered reviews to `POST /repos/{o}/{r}/stacks`, bottom first - the order the stack lands in. An existing stack is extended via `/stacks/{n}/add` rather than replaced; an unchanged one makes no call. - **Merges** it GitHub's way: a stacked pull request cannot go through the endpoint `gh pr merge` uses, so `merge` uses `PUT /pulls/{n}/merge-async` and polls the returned uuid to completion. - **Stops retargeting** what GitHub owns: a stacked pull request's base cannot be changed by hand, because GitHub moves each layer itself as the one below lands. `submit` and `cleanup` say so instead of claiming a change git-stk did not make. - `repair` prefers the stack GitHub records to the review base and to ancestry - an ordering that was *stated* rather than inferred, survives a wiped `.git/config`, and is still right where a review has since been retargeted. ## Why merge and retarget are in the same PR Registering is not additive. I probed it live on `git-stk-test-gh` before writing any of it, and both of these are hard refusals: ``` gh pr merge -> This pull request is part of a stack and must be merged using the asynchronous merge REST API. (mergePullRequest) gh pr edit --base -> Cannot change the base branch because the pull request is part of a stack. (updatePullRequest) ``` So registration alone would have handed an opted-in user a broken `git stk merge` **and** a broken `git stk submit`. The three land together or not at all. Findings written up in #306. ## Verified end to end Against real GitHub, with `stk.githubStacks = true`: ``` git stk submit --stack -> created #4 -> main, #5 -> e2e/one, registered #4 #5 as a stack GET /stacks -> {"number":6,"base":"main","layers":[4,5]} git stk submit --stack -> idempotent: no re-registration, no retarget attempted git stk merge -y -> merged #4 via merge-async; GitHub retargeted #5 to main git stk merge -y -> merged #5; stack complete ``` Test repo left clean afterwards - branches deleted, no open PRs. ## Not changed The local side. `restack`, `absorb`, worktrees, `undo`, and the `branch..stk*` metadata are all still git-stk's, and the cross-provider stack overview stays - it carries merged and closed history the native map does not, and GitLab and Gitea have no equivalent. Closes #306 - 🟣 ~~[fix(github): close the review follow-ups across the stack (#326)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/326)~~ (merged) - 🟣 ~~[feat(guide): add a github tour for stacked pull requests (#325)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/325)~~ (merged) - 🟣 ~~[test(tests): cover GitHub's native stacks in the live e2e suite (#324)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/324)~~ (merged) - 🟣 ~~[feat(list): show a review's place in the platform's own stack (#323)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/323)~~ (merged) - 🟣 ~~[fix(stack): name the branch and parent in every adopt suggestion (#322)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/322)~~ (merged) - 🟣 ~~[feat(unstack): dissolve the platform's own stack (#321)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/321)~~ (merged) - 🟣 ~~[test(merge): cover merge --all and every async status for a stacked review (#320)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/320)~~ (merged) - 🟣 ~~[fix(github): a lone review is not a stack to register (#319)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/319)~~ (merged) - 🟣 ~~[feat(github): read GitHub's native stacks behind stk.githubStacks (#312)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/312)~~ (merged) 👈 - 🟣 ~~[fix(sync): sync adopts proper base branch (#310)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/310)~~ (merged) - 🟣 ~~[fix(stack): submit/merge now understand non-trunk stack parents better (#309)](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk/pull/309)~~ (merged) - `main` --- Stack managed by [git-stk](https://github.com/lararosekelley/git-stk)

expected.description: Native stack detection returns None whenever stk.githubStacks is off, so stacks created outside git-stk go unnoticed and merge and retarget are attempted the ordinary way, which GitHub refuses.

prior_bot.note: bot asked for the setting to gate more paths, not fewer
